question: Can explicit bilinear host-phage interactions improve on an additive model with identical genome-composition inputs?
scope: already-inspected computational development and published BASEL reference; no independent release or biological mechanism claim

representation.source: actual byte-verified DNA for all 177 original hosts and 94 original phages; same fixed within-contig strand-canonical fourmers
representation.preprocessing: fit separate mean and population standard deviation on unique fit host/phage assembly digests only; exact zero scales become one; no held-out or BASEL statistics
representation.unsupported: missing/changed sequence, mismatched feature schema or no valid windows blocks fitting/scoring; never synthesize a biological zero vector

training.labels: reconcile primary MLC through curate_mlc; positive iff observed MLC > 0; keep conflicting duplicate-genome observations
training.split: existing immutable i95_s42 crossed manifest only; no seed or threshold search
training.sensitivity_weighting: sequence_pair_equal using existing inverse exact-sequence-pair observation multiplicity; retain both

models.bilinear: c + a^T h + b^T p + h^T W p

training.objective: weighted mean [logaddexp(0,z)-y*z] + lambda/2 * squared L2 norm of all slopes, including W; intercept unpenalized
training.implementation: matrix-free exact bilinear gradients; no materialized row-by-18496 outer-product feature matrix
training.selection_metric: weighted raw-logit AP on cold-phage validation only, separately for each model and weighting
training.selection_tie_rule: prefer stronger L2 within AP tolerance; never use test or BASEL labels
training.initialization: all slopes zero; intercept logit of (weighted positives + 0.5)/(total weight + 1)
training.failure: record failure and stop; no post-result parameter, feature, seed or threshold changes
training.ranking_scores: raw logits; fixed feature-order accumulation so identical inputs retain exact ties; sigmoid is only for uncalibrated Brier/log-loss diagnostics

development_evaluation.primary_contrast: bilinear minus additive weighted AP on cold_phage test

bootstrap.unit: whole phage groups on cold_phage test; conditional on this inspected source and fitted models

development_evaluation.improvement_rule: positive primary AP-gain lower 95% conditional group-bootstrap bound; otherwise not established; report both weighting outcomes

full_refit_and_BASEL.refit: after validation-only hyperparameter selection, refit every model on all 16597 original observed pairs with new full-cohort scalers; no selection from development test outcomes
full_refit_and_BASEL.label_separation: BASEL labels enter evaluation only after every full-refit score matrix is generated
full_refit_and_BASEL.candidates: all 25 hosts x all 52 phages, never filter to observed pairs
full_refit_and_BASEL.features: use the 102 actual frozen 136-dimensional vectors and sequence-bound manifests from BASEL fixed controls, verifying all hashes and identities
full_refit_and_BASEL.assay_shift: training MLC-positive logits evaluated against published binary spot clearance; no calibrated probability or productive-infection mapping
full_refit_and_BASEL.primary_metric: macro-host Hit@2 identification bounds; K=1,3,5, test-cost and unknown/near-neighbour exposures secondary; same exact-tie convention as v2
comparators: new additive and phage-only learned models
full_refit_and_BASEL.delta_bounds: bilinear lower - additive upper, bilinear upper - additive lower; conservative outer bounds, not sharp paired-assignment or confidence intervals
full_refit_and_BASEL.release: no promotion on this already inspected reference; keep every failure and unfavorable result
